lem-2dyck-pcfg-prefix-mass-positive:
## Statement

Fix $p\in(0,1)$. Independently expand each nonterminal of the grammar $S\to(S)S$, $S\to[S]S$, $S\to\epsilon$ with respective probabilities $p/2,p/2,1-p$, and read the yield from left to right. Equivalently, start with an empty bracket stack and repeatedly choose an opening bracket of either type with probability $p/2$ each, pushing its type; with probability $1-p$, close the top bracket when the stack is nonempty, or emit $\mathtt{eos}$ and stop when it is empty. This defines a probability law on finite words followed by $\mathtt{eos}$ and on infinite bracket streams. For a valid bracket prefix $x$, let $o(x),c(x)$ and $h(x)=o(x)-c(x)$ denote its opening count, closing count and final stack height. Its cylinder probability is
$$
w_p(x)=(p/2)^{o(x)}(1-p)^{c(x)}.
$$
For every $k\ge0$, let $s_{p,k}=\sum_{|x|=k}w_p(x)$, summing over valid prefixes, and define $D_{p,k}(x)=w_p(x)/s_{p,k}$. Thus $D_{p,k}$ conditions only on having emitted at least $k$ bracket tokens, without conditioning on eventual termination or exact total length. The target after a sampled prefix is its ordinary next token in the same process. At positive height its law assigns $p/2$ to each opening type and $1-p$ to the matching closing type.

For $k\ge3$, let $E_k$ consist of prefixes whose last three symbols are an opening of type $a$, an opening of type $b$, and the closing of type $b$, with $a,b$ independently ranging over the two types. These prefixes have positive final height and end in a closing bracket. Flipping the opening type $a$ at position $k-2$ is a fixed-point-free involution of $E_k$ into equal-mass pairs; paired prefixes differ only at this nonfinal position and their top unmatched opening types are opposite. Moreover,
$$
D_{p,k}(E_k)=p^2(1-p)\frac{s_{p,k-3}}{s_{p,k}}\ge p^2(1-p)>0.
$$

The finite-word mass of a typed Dyck word of length $2m$ is $(p/2)^m(1-p)^{m+1}$. The total finite-word mass is $q_p=1$ for $p\le1/2$ and $q_p=(1-p)/p$ for $p>1/2$. After conditioning on eventual termination, the finite-word probability law and all its prefix laws are exactly those of the preceding process with parameter $a=pq_p=\min(p,1-p)$; consequently its survival-conditioned prefixes have the same pairing bound $a^2(1-a)$. Conditioning instead on exact word length $2m$ yields the uniform law on typed Dyck words of that length, independently of $p$; that conditioning is different and does not retain the displayed next-token probabilities.
def-scaled-dot-product-attention:
## Definition

Let $n_q,n_k,d_k,d_v$ be positive integers, let $Q\in\mathbb R^{n_q\times d_k}$ and $K\in\mathbb R^{n_k\times d_k}$ be query and key matrices, and let $V\in\mathbb R^{n_k\times d_v}$ be a value matrix. For a real matrix $S$ with $n_q$ rows and $n_k$ columns, define its row softmax by $\operatorname{softmax}_{\rm row}(S)_{ij}=\exp(S_{ij})/\sum_{\ell=1}^{n_k}\exp(S_{i\ell})$. The scaled dot-product attention output is

$$
\operatorname{Attn}(Q,K,V)=\operatorname{softmax}_{\rm row}\!\left(\frac{QK^{\mathsf T}}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V\in\mathbb R^{n_q\times d_v}.
$$

Each output row is the weighted average of the value rows, with weights given by the softmax of that query's scaled dot products with all keys. A mask is an array $M\in(\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\})^{n_q\times n_k}$ whose entries are $0$ for allowed query-key pairs and $-\infty$ for disallowed pairs; masked attention replaces the score matrix by $QK^{\mathsf T}/\sqrt{d_k}+M$ before row softmax and is defined only when every row has at least one allowed key. Here $\exp(-\infty)=0$.
def-positional-encoding-and-causal-mask:
## Definition

For a sequence of length $n$ with $d$-dimensional token representations, a positional encoding is a fixed or trainable matrix $P\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$ added rowwise to the token matrix $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$, giving $X+P$. One fixed choice, with positions $s\in\mathbb N_0$ and coordinates indexed from $0$, is $P_{s,2r}=\sin(s/10000^{2r/d})$ and $P_{s,2r+1}=\cos(s/10000^{2r/d})$ whenever the indicated coordinate is less than $d$.

For decoder self-attention on $n$ positions, the causal mask is $M\in(\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\})^{n\times n}$ with $M_{ij}=0$ when $j\le i$ and $M_{ij}=-\infty$ when $j>i$. Thus query position $i$ can use keys at positions $1,\ldots,i$ and cannot use a future position; every row has an allowed key because $M_{ii}=0$.
lem-paired-crossentropy-mixture-bound:
## Statement

Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet of size $m\ge1$. Let $r,s,q,q'$ be probability vectors on $\Sigma$, and let $\epsilon\ge0$ satisfy $\|q-q'\|_1\le\epsilon$. For $\operatorname{CE}(r,q)=-\sum_a r(a)\log q(a)$, with value $+\infty$ if $r(a)>0=q(a)$, and $H(r)=-\sum_{a:r(a)>0}r(a)\log r(a)$, the paired loss satisfies

$$
\frac12\operatorname{CE}(r,q)+\frac12\operatorname{CE}(s,q')\ge H\!\left(\frac{r+s}{2}\right)-\log(1+m\epsilon).
$$

In particular, predictions whose $\ell^1$ distance tends to zero cannot have asymptotic paired loss below the entropy of the mean target law.
def-multihead-self-attention:
## Definition

Let $h,d_q,d_k,d_v,d_h,d_{vh},d_o,n_q,n_k$ be positive integers. For query, key, and value matrices $Q\in\mathbb R^{n_q\times d_q}$, $K\in\mathbb R^{n_k\times d_k}$, and $V\in\mathbb R^{n_k\times d_v}$, choose matrices $W_i^Q\in\mathbb R^{d_q\times d_h}$, $W_i^K\in\mathbb R^{d_k\times d_h}$, and $W_i^V\in\mathbb R^{d_v\times d_{vh}}$ for each head $i=1,\ldots,h$, and choose $W^O\in\mathbb R^{h d_{vh}\times d_o}$. The $i$-th head is

$$
H_i=\operatorname{Attn}(QW_i^Q,KW_i^K,VW_i^V)\in\mathbb R^{n_q\times d_{vh}},
$$

where $\operatorname{Attn}$ is scaled dot-product attention, with any chosen mask applied to its score matrix. Multi-head attention is

$$
\operatorname{MHA}(Q,K,V)=\operatorname{Concat}_{\rm feature}(H_1,\ldots,H_h)W^O\in\mathbb R^{n_q\times d_o}.
$$

Self-attention is the specialization $Q=K=V=X$ for a single token matrix $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$; each row is one token representation. Unmasked self-attention permits every query row to use every key row. Masked self-attention applies one specified mask to every head.
def-hahn-hard-soft-attention-sequence-mo:
## Definition

Let $\Sigma$ be a finite token alphabet, let $\mathtt{eos}\notin\Sigma$ be an end-of-sequence symbol, and let $d,L,H\ge1$ be fixed integers. For each length $n\ge1$, an input is $(x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1},\mathtt{eos})$. A symbol embedding assigns a vector $v_a\in\mathbb R^d$ to each $a\in\Sigma\cup\{\mathtt{eos}\}$; a positional embedding sequence assigns $p_i\in\mathbb R^d$ independent of the input symbols. A fixed shared input map gives $y_i^{(0)}=f_{\rm in}(v_{x_i},p_i)$. For each layer $k=1,\ldots,L$ and head $h=1,\ldots,H$, a fixed score map $s_{k,h}:\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ gives scores $a_{i,j}^{(k,h)}=s_{k,h}(y_i^{(k-1)},y_j^{(k-1)})$ for every query position $i$ and key position $j$. In the soft model, $\widehat a_{i,\cdot}^{(k,h)}=\operatorname{softmax}(a_{i,\cdot}^{(k,h)})$. In the hard model, $\widehat a_{i,j}^{(k,h)}=1$ at the smallest index $j$ attaining $\max_{r\le n}a_{i,r}^{(k,h)}$ and is $0$ at other indices. With fixed value maps $V_{k,h}:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ and fixed positionwise maps $F_k:(\mathbb R^d)^{H+1}\to\mathbb R^d$, the update is

$$
b_{i,k,h}=\sum_{j=1}^{n}\widehat a_{i,j}^{(k,h)}V_{k,h}(y_j^{(k-1)}),\qquad y_i^{(k)}=F_k(y_i^{(k-1)},b_{i,k,1},\ldots,b_{i,k,H}).
$$

Each score, value, and positionwise map is shared across positions and is fixed independently of $n$. In the hard-attention limit theorem, the score, value, and positionwise maps may be arbitrary fixed maps; no activation-function or parameter-norm bound is imposed. For the soft-influence theorem below, each score is a scaled dot product of fixed linear query and key projections, each value map is a fixed linear map, the token and positional embeddings are uniformly bounded over all positions and lengths, and every positionwise map is globally Lipschitz. A hard-attention recognizer classifies the input from $y_n^{(L)}$ after reading $\mathtt{eos}$. A soft next-token predictor applies a fixed linear logit map and softmax to $y_n^{(L)}$ to obtain a probability vector on a fixed finite alphabet.
lem-hard-attention-depth-reduction:
## Statement

Fix a finite input alphabet $\Sigma$ with $s=|\Sigma|\ge2$, a hard-attention model with fixed $H\ge1$ heads per position and $L\ge1$ layers, and an integer $c\ge1$. An input restriction at length $n$ assigns each input position either $*$ (free) or a fixed symbol of $\Sigma$. Say that a layer-zero activation depends on at most $c$ free positions if, with the restriction fixed, its value is determined by at most $c$ of the remaining free input symbols. Suppose the current restriction leaves at least $Cn$ positions free for every sufficiently large $n$, where $0<C\le1$, and every layer-zero activation depends on at most $c$ free positions. For every $0<C'<C$, there are an integer $c'\ge1$ and a refinement, for every sufficiently large $n$, that leaves at least $C'n$ positions free and preserves the model's output on every completion, while absorbing the first remaining attention layer into new layer-zero activations that each depend on at most $c'$ original input positions. Repeating this conclusion through the fixed $L$ layers gives a restriction with at least $C'n$ free positions on which the output depends on at most a constant number of original input positions. The constants and the length threshold may depend on the fixed model, $c,C,C'$, but not on $n$.
thm-hard-attention-languages:
## Statement

Let $\mathrm{PARITY}=\{w\in\{0,1\}^*: w\text{ contains an even number of }1\text{s}\}$. Let $\mathrm{2DYCK}$ be the language over $\{(,),[,]\}$ of words whose brackets are correctly balanced and properly nested by type. No fixed finite-depth hard-attention sequence model with a fixed finite number of heads, fixed maps independent of input length, and a fixed classification readout from its end-marker state classifies every sufficiently long input exactly as a member or nonmember of $\mathrm{PARITY}$; no such model recognizes $\mathrm{2DYCK}$ either. Exact recognition means that the model's binary output equals the language membership indicator for every input word, with the end marker appended before the model is evaluated.
lem-soft-attention-one-symbol-influence:
## Statement

Fix a finite token alphabet and a fixed soft-attention sequence model with $L$ layers, $H$ heads per layer, fixed query/key/value matrices, and positionwise maps that are globally Lipschitz. Assume the token embeddings are bounded, the positional embeddings satisfy $\sup_i\|p_i\|_2<\infty$, and all model parameters are independent of the input length $n$. For two length-$n$ inputs with the same end marker at position $n$ and differing in only one token at a position $i<n$, there is a constant $C<\infty$, depending only on these bounds, matrices, maps, $L$, and $H$, such that their final hidden states satisfy

$$
\|y_n^{(L)}(x)-y_n^{(L)}(x')\|_2\le \frac{C}{n}.
$$

If a fixed globally Lipschitz map followed by softmax converts the final hidden state to next-token probabilities, then another constant $C'<\infty$ with the same allowed dependence satisfies $\|q_n(x)-q_n(x')\|_1\le C'/n$. No bound is asserted when the changed symbol is the final end marker, or when the number of layers, matrices, or their norms vary with $n$.
thm-soft-attention-parity-chance-limit:
## Statement

Fix $p\in(0,1)$. Generate a bit string by a two-state process whose state is the parity of the number of emitted $1$s: in the even state it terminates with probability $p$, and otherwise emits $0$ or $1$ with probability $(1-p)/2$ each; in the odd state it emits $0$ or $1$ with probability $1/2$ each and cannot terminate. For each $n\ge2$, let $D_n$ be the law of length-$(n-1)$ prefixes conditional on the process emitting at least $n-1$ bits, and ask a fixed soft-attention model to predict the next symbol in $\{\mathtt{eos},0,1\}$ from that prefix followed by the end marker. Let $r_x$ be the true next-symbol distribution and let $q_n(x)$ be the model's predicted distribution. Define cross-entropy by $\operatorname{CE}(r,q)=-\sum_a r(a)\log q(a)$, with value $+\infty$ if $r(a)>0=q(a)$, and entropy by $H(r)=-\sum_{a:r(a)>0}r(a)\log r(a)$. Then every fixed soft-attention model satisfying the one-symbol influence hypotheses has

$$\liminf_{n\to\infty}\mathbb E_{x\sim D_n}\operatorname{CE}(r_x,q_n(x))\ge H(u),\qquad u(\mathtt{eos})=p/2,\quad u(0)=u(1)=(2-p)/4.$$
A constant predictor $q_n(x)=u$ attains $H(u)$ for every $n$, so $H(u)$ is the sharp unigram chance level. An arbitrary fixed predictor may have greater cross-entropy; this result gives no soft-attention exact-classification impossibility theorem.
alg-transformer-forward-pass:
## Definition

**Inputs:** A nonempty source token sequence $(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$, a target prefix $(y_0,\ldots,y_{m-1})$ with $m\ge1$ and a start token $y_0$, source and target embedding maps into $\mathbb R^d$, positional encoding matrices of compatible shapes, a finite encoder stack, a finite decoder stack, and a linear output map to a finite vocabulary of logits. Each layer has the parameters and conventions in the transformer encoder/decoder definition. All self-attention and cross-attention masks must leave at least one allowed key in every query row.

**Procedure:**

1. Embed each source token and add its positional vector to form $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$.
2. Apply the encoder layers in order to $X$ and call the final matrix $E\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$.
3. Embed each target-prefix token and add its positional vector to form $U\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}$.
4. Apply each decoder layer in order. In every decoder layer, use the causal mask on decoder self-attention, use the current decoder rows as queries and $E$ as keys and values for cross-attention, and then apply the positionwise feedforward sublayer.
5. Apply the output linear map to each final decoder row and apply softmax over vocabulary coordinates. Return the encoder matrix $E$, the final decoder hidden matrix, and the rowwise next-token probability matrix.

**Outputs:** The source representations, decoder representations, and one probability vector for each target-prefix position. At position $i$, the decoder self-attention calculation uses only target-prefix positions $j\le i$; the encoder cross-attention may use every source position.
thm-transformer-permutation-equivariance:
## Statement

Let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$ be a sequence matrix whose rows are token representations, and let $P$ be any $n\times n$ permutation matrix. Every finite composition $T$ of position-shared encoder layers built from unmasked multi-head self-attention, residual additions, rowwise layer normalization, and a shared positionwise feedforward map, with no positional encoding, satisfies

$$
T(PX)=P\,T(X).
$$

For a fixed attention mask $M$, the corresponding layer satisfies $\operatorname{Layer}_{PMP^{\mathsf T}}(PX)=P\operatorname{Layer}_{M}(X)$. Hence a fixed mask preserves only the permutations that leave $M$ unchanged. The standard causal mask $M_{ij}=0$ for $j\le i$ and $M_{ij}=-\infty$ for $j>i$ is preserved only by the identity permutation.
lem-soft-2dyck-crossentropy-gap-paired-p:
## Statement

Fix $p\in(0,1)$ and let $D_n$ be a probability law on valid length-$(n-1)$ prefixes over $\{(,),[, ]\}$. Let $E_n$ be a union of disjoint equal-mass pairs $\{x,x'\}$ in the support of $D_n$ such that each prefix in a pair ends in a closing bracket and has positive stack height after that bracket; $x'$ is obtained by changing the type of the top unmatched opening bracket in $x$, at a position before the final prefix symbol. Assume that, conditional on $x$, the next-symbol law assigns probability $p/2$ to each opening bracket and probability $1-p$ to the closing bracket matching its top unmatched opening, and that the law conditional on $x'$ swaps the two possible closing-bracket types while leaving the opening probabilities unchanged. If $D_n(E_n)\ge P_0>0$ for all sufficiently large $n$, then every fixed soft-attention predictor satisfying the one-symbol influence hypotheses has

$$
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\bigl(\mathcal L_n-\mathcal L_n^*\bigr)\ge P_0(1-p)\log 2,
$$

where $\mathcal L_n$ is expected next-symbol cross-entropy and $\mathcal L_n^*=\mathbb E_{x\sim D_n}H(r_x)$ is the optimal conditional cross-entropy. This lemma requires the positive-mass paired-prefix hypothesis; it does not assert that a particular PCFG supplies that hypothesis.
thm-transformer-formal-language-limits:
## Statement

For PARITY, whose members are the bit strings with an even number of $1$s, no fixed finite-depth hard-attention sequence model with fixed parameters recognizes every sufficiently long input exactly. For 2DYCK, whose words are correctly balanced and properly nested strings over two bracket types, no such hard-attention model recognizes the language. In both cases the model appends an end marker before classification.

For all soft-attention conclusions below, fix the parameter matrices, depth, and number of heads independently of length; use scaled dot-product scores with fixed linear query/key/value maps, uniformly bounded token and positional embeddings combined by addition, globally Lipschitz positionwise maps, and a fixed globally Lipschitz logit readout followed by softmax. Under these one-symbol influence assumptions, the parity source process with fixed $p\in(0,1)$ has sharp unigram cross-entropy level
$$
H(u),\qquad u(\mathtt{eos})=p/2,\quad u(0)=u(1)=(2-p)/4.
$$
Every such predictor has limiting lower cross-entropy at least $H(u)$, and the constant predictor $u$ attains it.

For the 2DYCK PCFG with rules $S\to(S)S$ and $S\to[S]S$ each of probability $p/2$, and $S\to\epsilon$ of probability $1-p$, fix any $p\in(0,1)$. Read its left-to-right output as a finite or infinite bracket stream; sample a length-$k$ prefix conditional on at least $k$ bracket tokens having been emitted, and predict the ordinary next token, without conditioning on exact total length. Every fixed soft-attention predictor satisfying these one-symbol influence assumptions has
$$
\liminf_{k\to\infty}(\mathcal L_{p,k}-\mathcal L_{p,k}^*)\ge p^2(1-p)^2\log 2>0,
$$
where $\mathcal L_{p,k}$ is its expected next-token cross-entropy under this prefix law and $\mathcal L_{p,k}^*$ is the corresponding optimal conditional cross-entropy.

The PCFG is a probability law on finite words precisely when $p\le1/2$. For all $p\in(0,1)$ its finite output can instead be conditioned on eventual termination. For that finite-word probability law, sample prefixes conditional on reaching length $k$ and predict the next token without any additional length conditioning. The same positive-gap conclusion holds with $p$ replaced by $a=\min(p,1-p)$:
$$
\liminf_{k\to\infty}(\mathcal L^{\mathrm{fin}}_{p,k}-(\mathcal L^{\mathrm{fin}}_{p,k})^*)\ge a^2(1-a)^2\log 2>0.
$$
For $p\le1/2$ these two prefix laws agree. At $p=1/2$ finite words have infinite expected length, but the prefix bounds still hold. For $p>1/2$ the first law includes nonterminating streams and the second conditions them away; neither is an unconditioned probability distribution on finite words with the original parameter $p$. These are cross-entropy limits, not exact-classification impossibility theorems.
lem-yun-transformer-grid-lookup:
## Statement

Let $d\ge1$, $n\ge2$, $m\ge2$ be integers, set $\delta=1/m$ and $q=\delta^{-d}$, and assume $n\le q$. Define
$$G_\delta=\{0,\delta,\ldots,1-\delta\}^{d\times n},\qquad G_\delta^+=\{-\delta^{-nd},0,\delta,\ldots,1-\delta\}^{d\times n}.$$
Let $\widehat G_\delta$ consist of those $L\in G_\delta$ whose columns are pairwise distinct. For column-token matrices $Z\in\mathbb R^{d\times n}$, consider finite compositions of residual attention updates
$$Z\longmapsto Z+\sum_{h=1}^{2}o_h(v_h^{\mathsf T}Z)\, \operatorname{hmax}\!\left((k_h^{\mathsf T}Z)^{\mathsf T}(r_h^{\mathsf T}Z+b_h\mathbf1_n^{\mathsf T})\right)$$
and residual tokenwise updates
$$
Z\longmapsto Z+w\,\phi(v^{\mathsf T}Z+b\mathbf1_n^{\mathsf T}),
$$
where all displayed vectors and scalars are fixed across columns, $\operatorname{hmax}$ assigns equal weights to all maximizing entries in each column, and each scalar $\phi$ is piecewise affine on at most three intervals with at least one constant piece. If $A:\widehat G_\delta\to\mathbb R^{d\times n}$ satisfies $A(LP)=A(L)P$ for every column-permutation matrix $P$, then such a composition maps each $L\in\widehat G_\delta$ to $A(L)$ and each $L\in G_\delta^+\setminus\widehat G_\delta$ to $0$.

There is also a position-tagged version. For each $j=1,\ldots,n$, let
$$J_j=\{j-1,j-1+\delta,\ldots,j-\delta\}^d,\qquad G_{\delta,\mathrm{pos}}=J_1\times\cdots\times J_n,$$
where the $j$th factor specifies column $j$. For every function $A:G_{\delta,\mathrm{pos}}\to\mathbb R^{d\times n}$, with no permutation condition, a finite composition of the same updates maps each $L\in G_{\delta,\mathrm{pos}}$ to $A(L)$.
lem-dense-attention-cost-and-path-length:
## Statement

Use the standard dense self-attention interaction with $n$ token rows, model width $d$, and $h$ heads whose total query/key/value width is $d$ (for example, $h$ heads of width $d/h$ when $h$ divides $d$). Counting scalar multiply-add operations in the direct matrix implementation, forming all query-key scores and applying the resulting dense weight matrix to all value rows costs $O(n^2d)$ per attention sublayer; row softmax adds $O(n^2)$. Every query position has a direct value path from every key position, so one unmasked self-attention sublayer gives path length one between any input token value and any output token. A fixed stack of $L$ such layers has a position-to-position path of at most $L$ attention edges, independent of $n$.

If each query, key, value, and output projection is a dense $d\times d$ linear map and the tokenwise feedforward width is $d_{\rm ff}$, those operations add $O(nd^2+ndd_{\rm ff})$ work per full Transformer layer. Thus the $O(n^2d)$ claim concerns the dense all-pairs attention interaction used in the source comparison; it does not assert that projections or the feedforward sublayer have that cost, and it makes no claim about sparse attention, linear attention, training work, memory traffic, or hardware speed.
thm-fixed-width-transformer-lp-universal:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, fix integers $d\ge1$ and $n\ge2$, and fix $1\le p<\infty$. For a matrix $Y\in\mathbb R^{d\times n}$, let $\|Y\|_p=(\sum_{r=1}^d\sum_{j=1}^n|Y_{rj}|^p)^{1/p}$, and for measurable maps on $\mathbb R^{d\times n}$ define
$$
d_p(f,g)=\left(\int_{\mathbb R^{dn}}\|f(X)-g(X)\|_p^p\,dX\right)^{1/p},
$$
using $dn$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Let $\mathcal T^{2,1,4}$ be the finite compositions of the two-head, head-size-one Yun blocks with tokenwise ReLU feedforward width four and no layer normalization. If $f:\mathbb R^{d\times n}\to\mathbb R^{d\times n}$ is continuous, has compact support, and satisfies $f(XP)=f(X)P$ for every $n\times n$ permutation matrix $P$, then for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $g\in\mathcal T^{2,1,4}$ with $d_p(f,g)<\varepsilon$.

For every compact $K\subseteq\mathbb R^{d\times n}$ and every continuous $f:K\to\mathbb R^{d\times n}$, with no permutation condition, there are a trainable positional matrix $E\in\mathbb R^{d\times n}$ and $g\in\mathcal T^{2,1,4}$ such that
$$
\left(\int_K\|f(X)-g(X+E)\|_p^p\,dX\right)^{1/p}<\varepsilon.
$$
